concepts.def: Differences within a species (genetic and environmental).
Change in a population over generations.
Grouping organisms by shared, evolutionary features.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity & Natural Resources — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity & Natural Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity & Natural Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Higher Simpson's diversity index D indicates:
options: Lower biodiversity
Higher biodiversity
No biodiversity
Same biodiversity

mcqs.q: Captive breeding is an example of:
options: In situ conservation
Ex situ conservation
Reforestation
Succession

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.

mcqs.q: What actually changes during natural selection in a population?
options: The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Individual organisms change their own genes to adapt.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
The frequencies of alleles in the population's gene pool change across generations.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Simpson's index”?
options: Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Species richness”?
options: Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.
Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Conservation”?
options: Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.
The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.
Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Captive breeding”?
options: Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.
Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Biodiversity”?
options: The number of different species in a community, ignoring relative abundance.
Protection and management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity for future generations.
Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Species evenness”?
options: Relative abundance of different species in a community; high if abundances are similar.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², a measure of biodiversity including both richness and evenness.
Variety of living organisms; measured at species, genetic and ecosystem levels.
Ex situ conservation; breeding endangered species in captivity to maintain gene pools and reintroduce them.

free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.
